instruction:
You are tasked with designing a data buffer that can store and retrieve data using Verilog. The buffer should have a capacity of DEPTH and have the ability to read and write data. The buffer should also have full and empty signals that indicate when the buffer is full or empty, respectively. You will be given a code snippet that includes a module with several sub-modules for implementing the buffer. Your task is to complete the code to implement the buffer.

The module includes a RAM instantiation that is used as a data buffer. The RAM has a memory size of DEPTH and an address width of L. The data width is specified by the dat_width parameter. The RAM has an input port for writing data (dat_i), an output port for reading data (dat_o), and input ports for the write and read addresses (adr_wr_i and adr_rd_i, respectively). The module also includes input ports for clock (CLK), write enable (Wren), and read enable (Rden).

The module has a READ_DATA sub-module that reads data from the RAM and outputs it on the Dataout port. The sub-module should be triggered on the positive edge of the clock or the reset signal (Rst). If the reset signal is high or the read enable signal is low, the Dataout port should output 0. If the read enable signal is high, the Dataout port should output the data from the RAM.

The module also has a STATUS_COUNTER sub-module that keeps track of the number of data elements stored in the buffer. The sub-module should be triggered on the positive edge of the clock or the reset signal (Rst). If the reset signal is high, the status counter should be set to 0. If a read command occurs, the status counter should be decreased by one. If a write command occurs and the buffer is not full, the status counter should be increased by one. If a write command occurs and the buffer is full, the status counter should remain the same. If both a read and a write command occur at the same time, the status counter should increase and decrease by one, so no action is required.

The module also has a FULL_EMPTY sub-module that generates full and empty signals based on the status counter. The sub-module should be triggered on the positive edge of the write clock (Wrclk) or the reset signal (Rst). If the reset signal is high, the full signal should be 0 and the empty signal should be 1. If the status counter is equal to DEPTH-1, the full signal should be 1 and the empty signal should be 0. If the status counter is equal to 0, the full signal should be 0 and the empty signal should be 1. Otherwise, the full signal should be 0 and the empty signal should be 0.

Your task is to complete the module by implementing the READ_DATA, STATUS_COUNTER, and FULL_EMPTY sub-modules.
